mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 4% in the month prior to the prediction date is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to reduced risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the mean of the prior 30 months (t-test p > 0.05) during the same policy regime.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS (labor market strength) combined with a decline in UNRATE (labor participation) predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as strong hiring outpaces wage growth pressures.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases in the same month
regime_hint: expanding labor market with soft wage growth
failure_condition: Rank IC of the interaction < 0.05 over the 60-day horizon in 80% of similar labor market regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in HOUST (residential construction) above the prior 3 months' average coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as building activity signals economic expansion.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative or flat during the 3-month period following the peak in HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) exceeding 2% suggests supply-side weakness, predicting a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during the identified contraction period.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 1% for three consecutive months during a low-inflation regime, the S&P 20-day forward return tends to be positive as expectations of future rate cuts support equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for 3 consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < 210 (low inflation signal)
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day rolling mean during the same conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 4% combined with a decline in PAYEMS predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as weak labor market conditions suppress investor confidence.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% while PAYEMS falls in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly worse than the prior 6-month average in similar labor regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in GDPC1 (GDP momentum) above the 12-month moving average predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as strong demand supports valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day returns fail to outperform the 12-month rolling mean during the momentum period.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in both INDPRO and RSAFS (retail sales) exceeding 3% indicate supply-side softness, predicting a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.15) in analogous contraction regimes.
